skill.name: airtable-automation
skill.description: Automate Airtable records, schemas, filters, and comments through Rube MCP with schema-first workflows.
skill.summary: Schema-first Airtable automation through Rube MCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code around tool names, parameters, and Airtable formula examples. The real risks are the disclosed external Rube MCP dependency and workflows that can modify or delete Airtable data. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Document that Rube MCP is a third-party endpoint and advise users to verify OAuth scopes before connecting Airtable.
Require an explicit confirmation step or dry-run plan before deletes, batch updates, and schema changes.
Tell users to validate field names and quote formula values before passing filters to Airtable tools.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Airtable connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `airtable`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
- `tableIdOrName`: Table ID (starts with 'tbl') or table name
- `fields`: Object mapping field names to values
- `typecast`: Set true for automatic type conversion
- `fields`: Array of field names to return
- `maxRecords`: Max total records across all pages
- Field names in formulas must be wrapped in `{}` and match schema exactly
- String values must be quoted: `{Status}='Active'` not `{Status}=Active`
- `options`: Type-specific options (choices for select, precision for number)
- Single quotes in values: double them (`{Name}='John''s Company'`)
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k

content.value_statement: Airtable work can slow teams when records, fields, and filters need manual updates. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through schema-first Airtable actions using Rube MCP.
actual_capabilities: Discover Airtable bases and inspect table schemas before making changes.
List, filter, sort, and paginate records with Airtable formulas.
Create, update, and delete records, including small batch operations.
Create fields and update field or table metadata where the API supports it.
List comments on Airtable records through the connected MCP tools.
limitations: Requires an active Rube MCP connection and authorized Airtable account.
Batch create, update, and delete actions are limited to 10 records per request.
Computed fields, such as formulas and rollups, cannot be created through the API.
The skill provides workflows; it does not validate your Airtable permissions.

use_cases.title: Operations Data Cleanup
use_cases.description: Find stale Airtable records, review proposed changes, and apply approved updates in small batches.

use_cases.title: Product Backlog Maintenance
use_cases.description: Filter product records by status, priority, or owner and update selected items after schema checks.

use_cases.title: Support Record Review
use_cases.description: List customer records, inspect comments, and prepare safe follow-up updates for support workflows.

prompt_templates.title: List My Bases
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Airtable automation skill to list available bases and explain which base matches my workspace goal.

prompt_templates.title: Find Records by Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Search my selected Airtable table for records where Status is Active. Show the matching record names and IDs.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Batch Records
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the schema, then prepare a safe plan to create these task records in Airtable. Ask before writing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Schema Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Airtable table schema, identify missing fields for our pipeline, and propose staged updates with rollback notes.

output_examples.input: Find open onboarding tasks in the HR base.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists matching records with names, owners, due dates, and record IDs for review.

output_examples.input: Add three campaign records after checking schema.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the schema, asks for approval, then reports created records and any validation issues.

output_examples.input: Review comments on a customer renewal record.
output_examples.output: The assistant retrieves recent comments and summarizes action items tied to the selected record.

best_practices: Call the tool search first so current Airtable tool schemas are used.
Confirm base, table, record IDs, and field names before writes.
Use small batches and review results before continuing.
anti_patterns: Do not delete or update records without explicit user confirmation.
Do not assume field names or select options without reading the schema.
Do not change filters or sort order while using pagination.

faq.question: Does this skill need an Airtable API key?
faq.answer: No. It uses Rube MCP and an authorized Airtable connection.

faq.question: Can it modify records?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create, update, and delete records when the connected Airtable account has permission.

faq.question: Can it manage Airtable schema?
faq.answer: It can create fields and update supported metadata, but it cannot create computed field types.

faq.question: How should large imports be handled?
faq.answer: Split large work into batches of 10 records or fewer and review each result.

faq.question: Does it work without Rube MCP?
faq.answer: No. The workflows require Rube MCP tools and an active Airtable connection.

faq.question: How can I prevent accidental deletions?
faq.answer: Ask for a dry run first and approve each delete or batch update action explicitly.
